home: I’m a student-athlete at Westford Academy who thrives on challenge and creativity, whether leading cross-country, coding late into the night, or bringing ideas to life through engineering and design. I consistently approach every project as an opportunity to build something meaningful, to push past “good enough,” and to use the time I have to create work that lasts.

projects.title:
Blackjack
(Java)
description: Designed and implemented a mostly full-featured Blackjack game in Java to practice advanced OOP design patterns, state management, and recursion in a game environment.
Game includes an 8-deck shoe, card shuffling, hit/stay/double/split/surrender logic, betting, dealer play, win detection, and bankroll.
Playable only via desktop Java due to GUI requirements. (I still want to port the implementation to React - next summer's project!)
I purposefully only used AI for UI elements, as my goal was to practice more advanced object-oriented programming.

projects.title: Neural Network (Python)
description: As part of a summer program at Tufts, leveraged AI to develop a self-driving race car simulation where a neural network learned optimal steering and acceleration using reinforcement learning. Tuned reward functions and visualized model convergence.

projects.title: Pac-Man (MIT Scratch)
projects.embed: <iframe src='https://scratch.mit.edu/projects/820510104/embed' allowtransparency='true' width='485' height='402' frameborder='0' scrolling='no' allowfullscreen></iframe>
description: This is a customized Pac-Man game comprised of 3 unique levels. Use the up, down, left, and right arrow keys to control Pac-Man. Collect all of the Food scattered throughout the map in order to advance to the next level within 90 seconds. There are two ghosts (Pinky and Clyde) that are programmed to randomly move through hallways. A second player can use the 'A' and 'D' controls to tell Clyde where to go relative to Clyde's position, and override the randomness of the movement. Each time you win a level, the next level will increase the speed for Pac-Man and the ghosts. Complete the 3 levels to win the game.

projects.title: Feed-the-Hole (MIT Scratch)
projects.embed: <iframe src='https://scratch.mit.edu/projects/815037201/embed' allowtransparency='true' width='485' height='402' frameborder='0' scrolling='no' allowfullscreen></iframe>
description: 'Feed The Hole' is similar to the common arcade game named 'Pop the Lock'. Instead of rotating in a circle this game goes side to side. Your objective is to precisely click the 'Space' key when the orange oval is over the black hole on the bar. Feed the oval into the hole 5 times within 20 seconds to gain 5 points and complete the level. Complete 3 levels to win the game.

essays.title: Left Behind
essays.description: A research paper examining the moral and strategic consequences of the U.S. military’s 'No Man Left Behind' policy, dedicated to my grand-uncle Allan P. Collamore.

essays.title: A Microcosm of America’s Grandeur and Shame
essays.description: An analytical essay using the 1904 St. Louis World’s Fair as a lens to examine how America’s celebration of progress and innovation coexisted with its legacy of racial hierarchy and imperialism—revealing a microcosm of both the nation’s grandeur and its shame.

essays.title: Pitfalls of Chasing an Unattainabile Dream on Social Media
essays.tagline: On illusion, aspiration, and the emptiness behind perfection
essays.description: A modern analysis of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby connecting 1920s façades of wealth, love, and beauty to today’s social media culture, revealing how the pursuit of curated perfection leads not to fulfillment, but to disillusionment and isolation.

essays.title: The Imperfect Green Revolution in India
essays.description: A research paper assessing how the Green Revolution transformed India’s agriculture, reducing famine while deepening social and environmental inequalities.

essays.title: Freedom from an Inescapable Prison of Society
essays.tagline: On confinement, awakening, and the cost of freedom
essays.description: An analytical essay on Kate Chopin’s The Awakening, exploring how Edna Pontellier’s struggle against the restrictive traditions of 1890s society (through motifs of birds, dreams, and the sea) reveals that true independence for women in her era was both revolutionary and tragically unattainable.

essays.title: Humanity in the Hands of the Government
essays.tagline: On control, conformity, and the loss of humanity
essays.description: An analytical essay on Aldous Huxley’s Brave New World, examining how government overreach and technological conditioning strip individuals of freedom, emotion, and identity, serving as a warning against trading authentic humanity for comfort and control.

essays.title: Stuck in the Quintessence of Childhood
essays.tagline: On preservation, innocence, and the necessity of change
essays.description: A literary analysis of J.D. Salinger’s The Catcher in the Rye, exploring how Holden Caulfield’s desire to preserve childhood innocence and resist risk reveals the futility of stagnation, and how embracing change is essential for growth and fulfillment.

essays.title: Napoloean Perpetuated the Goals of Enlightenment as a Power-Hungry Tyrant
essays.tagline: On ambition, reform, and the paradox of enlightened rule
essays.description: An essay exploring how Napoleon Bonaparte advanced Enlightenment ideals of progress, liberty, and reason through sweeping governmental, economic, and legal reforms, while simultaneously betraying them through his authoritarian ambition and conquest across Europe.

essays.title: The French Revolution Betrayed the Ideals of Liberty and Equality
essays.tagline: On revolution, reason, and the failure to uphold ideals
essays.description: A historical analysis arguing that the French Revolution, though inspired by Enlightenment principles of liberty and equality, ultimately betrayed them through chaos, violence, and exclusion—culminating in the Great Fear, the Reign of Terror, and the denial of women’s rights.

essays.title: Generational Effects of Racial Discrimination
essays.tagline: On systemic prejudice and inherited inequality
essays.description: An analytical essay examining how To Kill a Mockingbird reflects the enduring link between racial discrimination and generational inequity, connecting Atticus Finch’s defense of Tom Robinson to real-world injustices like Jim Crow laws and Japanese internment.
